question:
An 75-year-old woman is brought to the clinic by her son for a follow-up visit. She was discharged two
weeks ago after being treated for an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She
reports occasional lightheadedness when standing up from a sitting position but otherwise feels well.
Her son mentions that her hearing has worsened over the past few years. She lives with her husband,
who has been using a wheelchair since a motorcycle accident 38 years ago. Her medical history
includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, panic disorder, migraines, and insomnia. Her current
medications are albuterol, ipratropium bromide, fluoxetine, lisinopril, rosiglitazone, topiramate,
lorazepam, and over-the-counter fish oil supplements. Vital signs measured in the recumbent position
are within normal limits. Based on her current medication regimen, this patient is at the greatest risk for
which of the following? Answer Choices: (A) Worsening insomnia (B) Bone fractures (C) Hyperkalemia
(D) Constipation (E) Peripheral edema (F) Hypoglycemia (G) Prerenal azotemia (H) Renal calculi (I)
Orthostatic hypotension (J) Cognitive impairment
 A. Cognitive impairment
B. Hyperkalemia
C. Peripheral edema
D. Constipation
E. Hypoglycemia

F. Orthostatic hypotension
G. Bone fractures
H. Renal calculi
I. Prerenal azotemia
J. Worsening insomnia
